chain: Given a message, follow its replyOf edges up to the original post and return that post's id.
chain3: Given a message, follow its replyOf edges up to the original post, but at most three steps.
closure: Given a tag class, find all its subclasses at any depth, including the class itself.
edge_probe: Given two persons, check whether they know each other.
entry_eq: Given a first name, find the ids of all persons with that first name, using the value index.
entry_eq_scan: Given a first name, find the ids of all persons with that first name by reading every person, with no index.
entry_range: Given a date window, count the persons created in it, using the creation date index.
entry_range_scan: Given a date window, count the persons created in it by reading every person, with no index.
entrylabel_forum: Count all the forums in the graph by listing the vertices of the Forum type.
entrylabel_person: Count all the persons in the graph by listing the vertices of the Person type.
entrylabel_post: Count all the posts in the graph by listing the vertices of the Post type.
fof_posters_profile: Given a person, list the id and name of the authors of posts by friends and friends of friends who were born in 1985 or later.
hop1_edgefilter: Given a person, count their friendships that began before 2011, filtering on an edge property.
hop1_hascreator: Given a person, count the messages they created.
hop1_hasmember: Given a forum, count its members.
hop1_hastag: Given a tag, count the distinct posts, comments and forums that carry it.
hop1_knows: Given a person, count the people they know.
hop1_knows_out: Given a person, count the people they know through knows edges that start at them.
hop1_label: Given a person, count those of their messages that are posts, testing the type of each message.
hop1_msgs_content: Given a person, read the content of each of their messages and count them.
hop1_msgs_date: Given a person, count their messages created before 2011, reading only the creation date of each.
hop1_posts_props: Given a person, read all properties of each of their posts and count the posts.
hop1_propfilter: Given a person, count the people they know who were created before 2011, filtering on a vertex property.
hop1p1_knows: Given a person, read one property (first name) of each person they know.
hop1p3_knows: Given a person, read three properties of each person they know.
hop1p7_knows: Given a person, read all seven properties of each person they know.
hop1p_knows: Given a person, list the id, first name and last name of each person they know.
hop2_post_likers: Given a person, count the distinct people who liked their posts.
nhop1: Given a person, find the people exactly one knows-step away.
nhop2: Given a person, find the people exactly two knows-steps away, not counting anyone closer.
nhop2_hetero: Given a person, find the distinct tags on the messages they created.
nhop2p: Given a person, find the people exactly two knows-steps away and read their id, first name and last name.
nhop3: Given a person, find the people exactly three knows-steps away, not counting anyone closer.
nhop4: Given a person, find the people exactly four knows-steps away, not counting anyone closer.
nhop4p: Given a person, find the people exactly four knows-steps away and read their id, first name and last name.
nhop5: Given a person, find the people exactly five knows-steps away, not counting anyone closer.
nhop6: Given a person, find the people exactly six knows-steps away, not counting anyone closer.
point1: Given a person, read their first name (one property).
point4: Given a person, read four of their properties.
point7: Given a person, read all seven of their properties.
point_post: Given a post, read all of its properties, including the long content.
topk1: Given a date, find the newest message (post or comment) created before it, with its content.
topk10: Given a date, find the 10 newest messages (posts or comments) created before it, with their content.
topk100: Given a date, find the 100 newest messages (posts or comments) created before it, with their content.
topk10_scan: Find the 10 newest messages (posts or comments) by reading every message and sorting, with no date index.
